newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel attacks SPD leader's tax talks conditions.
newsitem.headline: Waigel attacks SPD leader's tax talks conditions.

text.p: Finance Minister Theo Waigel on Thursday criticised the conditions attached by opposition leader Oskar Lafontaine to cooperating on German tax reforms, saying they smacked of populism and would not help create jobs.

"I have the impression that he is purely interested in populism and playing to the gallery," Waigel said after Lafontaine set five conditions which the government must meet at talks next week for new tax talks to succeed.

Lafontaine, in an interview with the Bild daily, said that in order to win his approval, the coalition must accede to his demands to make it clear how much the tax reform will cost, cut entry-rate income tax, raise tax-free allowances and child benefits and cut social security charges this July.

Waigel, who has proposed a package of 30 billion marks in corporate and income tax cuts to take effect over the next two years, said Lafontaine's demands would do nothing to stimulate job-creating investment.

He said it was the "wrong signal" to raise child benefits instead of cutting taxes. "We need the tax reforms for investment -- now," Waigel said on the fringes of a meeting of his Christian Social Union (CSU) party here.

The cross-party talks resume next week after a hiatus to try and find a compromise which would avert a drawn-out battle in parliament, where Lafontaine's Social Democrats (SPD) can block most tax measures through their upper house majority.
